quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, what should you do?

options.text: Switch between low and high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: If your rear brake locks on a good surface, what should you do?

options.text: Let go of the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop. On a good surface, a locked rear wheel will not cause you to lose control as long as your motorcycle is upright and going straight.

questions.question: When turning left, what should you do?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle leans to turn. Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, where should you ride?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of the lane when passing parked cars. This helps you avoid doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling into the lane. Stay ready to change position as conditions change.

questions.question: When being passed, why should you not move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing.
The side closest to the passing vehicle is safer.
You will feel more wind blast on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This tempts the driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If you started a curve on the outside and no traffic is present when exiting, which way should you move?

options.text: Toward the center of the curve.
Toward the inside of the curve.
Toward the outside of the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the outside of the curve.
questions.explanation: Start on the outside of a curve to see better and turn more smoothly. Move toward the inside as you turn. As you exit, move back toward the outside. Always watch for changes in road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How should you approach angled railroad tracks?

options.text: Go straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight ahead in your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight ahead in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to cross at a right angle can push you into another lane, which is dangerous.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane give a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane gives motorcyclists three paths: the left, center, and right parts of the lane.

questions.question: For routine braking, what should you do?

options.text: Switch between front and rear brakes to save brake life.
Always use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which of these is NOT important?

options.text: It meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.correctAnswerText: It looks attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fits snugly, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or torn straps. Appearance is not important.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down to let the dog get close, then speed up and ride away.
Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to let the dog get close, then speed up and ride away.
questions.explanation: Dogs are attracted to motorcycles. Slow down and shift to a lower gear as the dog approaches. Then speed up and leave the dog behind.

questions.question: How should you brake when making a normal stop on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, apply both the front and rear brakes together. Also downshift as you brake.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to shake or wobble?

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle along the road?

options.text: Park at a 45-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Park at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Park at a 90-degree angle with the front wheel touching the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop your motorcycle?

options.text: Grab the front brake lever quickly.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
Apply increasing pressure to the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: For the best straight-line braking, apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. As your weight moves forward, you can use more front brake pressure and less rear brake pressure. Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: Who should set the pace for a group of motorcycle riders?

options.text: The riders just behind the leader

questions.correctAnswerText: The last rider
questions.explanation: The last rider should set the pace. This makes sure no riders get left behind.

questions.question: Which lane position is best for riding in general?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. A good rider changes position based on conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on a bridge above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: Where do oil drippings and debris collect in a lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: The middle portion
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Need less stopping distance than larger vehicles.
Need the same stopping distance as larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need the same stopping distance as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Riders must keep enough space to stop safely. Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as other vehicles.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing.
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers about a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When moving faster than a walk, your motorcycle leans to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn. This makes the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group of riders entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when entering curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is good for staying together while maintaining safe distance on straight roads.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, increase your following distance. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked up to stop more quickly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake immediately and re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake pressure. Then re-apply the brake gradually and gently.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the animal loses interest.
Slow down and downshift, then quickly accelerate away as the dog approaches.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and downshift, then quickly accelerate away as the dog approaches.
questions.explanation: If a dog approaches, slow down and downshift. As the dog gets close, quickly accelerate away.

questions.question: Which of the following protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn at this intersection.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply it.
Release the front brake immediately and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake and re-apply it immediately.

questions.question: What color are the signs that show the distance to the next exit on a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Signs that show where to go have green backgrounds with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: When your passenger is on the motorcycle, tell them to do everything except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move around while you are riding. This helps you focus on the road. Passengers should board after the engine starts. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not talk or move unnecessarily.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers to stay quiet and still while riding. Passengers should board after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers that:

options.text: The right lane is ending and traffic must move left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and traffic must move left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about dangers ahead. This sign tells you that the right lane is ending and you need to move left.

questions.question: If you are over 18 and have a motorcycle license:

options.text: You must wear a helmet when it is raining.
You must wear a helmet if you have a passenger.
You do not have to wear a helmet, but it is strongly recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: You do not have to wear a helmet, but it is strongly recommended.
questions.explanation: In Wisconsin, riders under 18 and those with a permit must wear a helmet. Riders over 18 with a license do not have to wear one, but helmets are strongly recommended for all riders.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you what is coming up. This sign tells you there is a stop sign ahead. Be ready to stop.

questions.question: Which surface is least likely to cause poor grip for motorcycles?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor grip. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers are all risky. Dry pavement is the safest.

questions.question: When riding on wet pavement, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Follow in the tire tracks of other vehicles.
Use only the front brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow in the tire tracks of other vehicles.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, avoid the oily center strip of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles for better grip.

questions.question: When going through a curve, you should:

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane the whole time.
Stay in the left part of the lane the whole time.
Stay in the right part of the lane the whole time.
Know that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to move to a different part of the lane when needed. The best way through a curve may not follow the exact curve of the road.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear.
Use the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.
